headline: Every bottle checked, not a sample.
formProduct: Juices, waters and coffee drinks in PET
label: #F4ECDD
heroLede: Bickford's PET line in Adelaide runs more than 20 drinks, from juices and flavoured waters to coffee with milk and coffee with almonds, in 250 mL, 500 mL and 1 L bottles, at up to 12,000 bottles an hour on the aseptic side. With that many changeovers, the label is what tells one bottle from the next. This is what a camera check could look like on your line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every cap is on, straight and fully closed. A loose cap on an aseptic drink means a spoiled bottle on the shelf and a complaint from the store.
labelLede: Coffee with milk and coffee with almonds share a bottle and look much the same at speed. A wrong label there is an undeclared allergen. The camera checks every bottle carries the right label for the run, straight and intact.
codeLede: The best-before and batch code has to be right and readable on every bottle. The system reads the printed code and compares it with the drink and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Cap offcuts, label backing and loose parts can end up on the conveyor. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a case.

vocab.alert: Four crooked caps in fifteen minutes on the aseptic line. Check the capper.
